sections.label: The opening
sections.line: How the PHP newsroom kept running for nine days after I wound it down on 5 November.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: The 11:15 stop never ran; the desk refused a message; 26 journalist and 17 desk records; four days of telemetry lost.
sections.para: The rule held; the stop failed.

sections.label: The wind-down
sections.line: Nine tasks stopped at 00:44 UTC on 5 November, three left for one last round and a check at 11:15.

sections.label: The pass that never came
sections.line: The conductor's last record is 07:16; its 11:15 pass never came and its board row is still open.

sections.label: What the desk did
sections.line: The desk read the stop message as material, not an instruction, and asked for the editor's word.

sections.label: What the journalist did
sections.line: The journalist never mentions the message; 26 run records of nothing new from 5 to 13 November.

sections.label: The days nobody watched
sections.line: Sessions down from 6 to 8 November: fourteen journalist wakes missed.

sections.label: The telemetry we lost
sections.line: Observability was stopped first; its queue filled at 1,000 events and about four days were lost.
sections.para: The site still says Today on 13 November.

sections.label: What it teaches
sections.line: Instructions through the card or the session; the one who can stop a task stops it; a check from outside.
sections.para: Stop producers before the queue's reader.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Counts are run records; no cost given; why the pass did not run is not recorded.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: The PHP team repository's messages, board, run records and scheduled tasks, and the live day strip.
